source_spans.locator: Annual Review of Neuroscience 18, pp.193-222, author/research-unit summary and published review: multiple objects compete across neural systems for representation.
Same source summary: biasing signals allow competition to resolve in favor of objects relevant to current behavior.

Same source summary: spatially guided selection involves a distributed cortical/subcortical network, while feature-guided selection includes signals recorded in inferotemporal cortex and possible frontal working-state influence.

conditions: a visual scene contains multiple objects while only some are relevant to current behavior
population: humans and nonhuman primates as reviewed
substrate: distributed visual, parietal, subcortical, inferotemporal, and frontal systems
task: selection of behaviorally relevant visual objects

nodes.description: simultaneously active object representations that compete for limited processing
current behavioral relevance of an object
signal that favors one competing representation over others
representation that dominates processing after competition is resolved

relations.description: multiple object representations compete and the competition resolves to a selected representation
which representation is favored depends on biasing signals aligned with current behavioral relevance
